about: What a model of [JEngine] will structurally be unable to predict, one record each: claim, mechanism, evidence, asserted_value, source. See felizjueves.literature.limits.

limits.claim: exact_given_inputs on jengine/table1 (FLOPs): no recovered set of inputs reproduces all 40 printed cells. The cut IS recovered (plan/recovery.py, two-ended nearest fill per direction, which also gives all 40 of Table 3); the sieve's inputs are not. Refused under the rules-only doctrine (#108): a per-cell fitted seed order is not admitted as a recovered input.
limits.mechanism: Table 1 is post-sieve, and the sieve's output depends on its seed order: an order of a batch's targets, up to 969! of them at L = 16, one batch. [JEngine, v2, §4.1] says the order moves FLOPs and node count by up to ~2%, and that the authors did not optimise it; they do not state the order they used. So the order is an unpublished input with no rule to recover it from, and the printed cells sit inside its spread. Also unpublished, and searched below: which other direction a re-parented child takes, how far the upward sweep deletes, and whether the walk is breadth- or depth-first.
limits.evidence: Every search below uses the recovered cut and the counting conventions #10 fixed (1/2/3 FLOPs per node by r_d; fundamentals with m > 0 are intermediates). (1) The literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order: 9/40 exact, (7,3) (7,6) (7,9) (8,6) (8,9) (9,6) (9,9) (10,9) (11,9). (2) The literal sieve over plan/recovery.py's 26 structured seed orders (hermite_targets and its reverse; |r| ascending or descending, then the components in each of the 6 axis orders, all ascending or all descending): best 17/40 ('|r| asc, then xzy desc'). (3) A scratch variant of the sieve, not kept in the repo, over those 26 orders x 7 re-expansion choices (smallest r_d', largest r_d', xyz, zyx, smallest r_d' ties to z, cyclic successor, cyclic predecessor) x 2 sweeps (every orphaned node, or only i and its parents upward) x breadth- or depth-first x [r-1d] or [r-2d] enqueued first: 1456 configurations, best 17/40 Table 1 together with 29/40 Table 2. (4) Random seed orders, each sieved twice (smallest- and largest-r_d' re-expansion): 6000 runs (3000 orders) at (7,1) and at (8,1) reach the printed pair in 3578 and 460 of them, so those cells ARE seed-order effects; 600 runs (300 orders) at (16,1) never reach it (best FLOPs 5666 against the printed 5633; the hermite order gives 5644), so the paper's order there is in the tail, and no rule this search knows names it. Bounded at that point on purpose: the remaining space is the factorial order space itself, and searching it for each cell would be a per-cell fit. (5) #108, THE WIDENED FAMILY: plan/recovery.py's seed_orders(widened=True), the 26 above plus 32 rules each with a stated rationale (FLOPs of the target's MILD closure asc/desc; out-degree of its MILD parents asc/desc; sieve-greedy, by how many of its parents already pass Alg. 3's test, desc/asc; direction-major by batch_direction in the 6 axis orders; max-then-mid component in the 4 sign combinations, '+max/-mid' being the predecessor tree's base rule), each with hermite and reversed-hermite tie-breaks: 58 orders, literal sieve, recovered cut. Table 3 stays 40/40 under every one. Best Table 1: 33/40, one order only, '+max/-mid, ties reversed' (max component ascending, middle descending, then reversed hermite position); the same order is the unique best on Table 2 (38/40). Its 7 Table 1 misses are (13,3) (14,3) (15,1) (15,3) (16,1) (16,3) (16,6), every one OVER the printed FLOPs (+0.11% to +0.32%), and its 2 Table 2 misses (15,3) (16,1) are both UNDER the printed intermediates: the residual has one sign per table, the same trade test_plan_sieve.py's anchors show for the hermite order, which points at a choice inside the sieve (re-expansion), not at the seed order. That order was picked by its score from 58 named rules, so 33 is itself a selection over rules; it is still a rule applied to every cell, and it does not reach 40. THE DECISION (#108): RULES ONLY. exact_given_inputs records rules the paper's numbers were produced by, the same for every cell; a per-cell fitted order is not admitted, not even under a separately named rule. Reasons: (a) the predecessor tree's per-cell orders show a fit exists (all 40 cells of Tables 1-3, 29 cells needing no transposition, the rest 1-5 swaps off its own '+max/-mid' rule, found by a beam search scored against the Article's numbers), but those values do not transfer (a different cut recovery and seed-order family), and a fit shows only that some order reproduces a number, which is evidence of nothing about the method; (b) the one-sign residual above says a fit here would absorb a systematic difference in the sieve into per-cell inputs, so the fitted record would be wrong about what it records. The 7 cells stand at their printed values.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the 31 cells above, under the recovered cut and the literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order; their printed values are taken from the table as published

limits.claim: exact_given_inputs on jengine/table2 (max intermediates per batch): no recovered set of inputs reproduces all 40 printed cells. The cut IS recovered (plan/recovery.py); the sieve's inputs are not. Refused under the rules-only doctrine (#108), as jengine/table1 is.
limits.mechanism: Table 2 is post-sieve, as Table 1 is, and the intermediates the sieve deletes depend on the same unpublished seed order ([JEngine, v2, §4.1]: up to ~2%, not optimised, not stated). The record for jengine/table1 gives the full argument; the search was one search scoring both tables.
limits.evidence: Same search as jengine/table1's record. (1) Literal sieve, hermite_targets seed: 17/40 exact, (7,3) (7,6) (7,9) (8,6) (8,9) (9,6) (9,9) (10,6) (10,9) (11,6) (11,9) (12,6) (12,9) (13,9) (14,9) (15,3) (15,9). (2) Best of the 26 structured seed orders with the literal sieve: 29/40 ('hermite-reversed'; '|r| asc, then xzy desc' gives 28). (3) Best of the 1456 scratch-variant configurations: 29/40. (4) Random seed orders: the printed (7,1) and (8,1) cells are reached; the printed (16,1) cell is not in 600 runs (range 1633-1666 against the printed 1647, together with FLOPs never at 5633). (5) #108's widened family of 58 seed-order rules (the jengine/table1 record has it in full): best 38/40, the unique best and the same order as Table 1's, '+max/-mid, ties reversed'; its misses (15,3) and (16,1) are both under the printed value (481 against 482, 1643 against 1647). Refused under the same rules-only decision, for the same reasons.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the 23 cells above, under the recovered cut and the literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order; their printed values are taken from the table as published

limits.claim: at_or_under on the searched board, jengine/table1 (FLOPs) and jengine/table2 (max intermediates): 21 cells of Table 1 and 3 of Table 2 stay over the printed value under the searched plans. Table 3 is at or under in all 40. Every residual cell is over by at most +2.04%, and all but one by at most +1.04%.
limits.mechanism: The printed cells are post-sieve, and the sieve's output depends on its seed order, which [JEngine, v2, §4.1] says moves FLOPs and node count by up to ~2%, was not optimised, and is not stated (the jengine/table1 exact_given_inputs record above has the full argument). The residual margins sit inside that spread: the paper's numbers are one draw from the seed-order space, and in these cells the draw is better than any order in the bounded family searched. Reaching it means searching the factorial order space per cell, which is a per-cell fit to the printed answer, not a generator choice. The one margin at the edge of the spread, (16, 1) Table 1 at +2.04%, is the objective's price: putting intermediates before FLOPs takes a seed order with 2 fewer intermediates and 104 more FLOPs; the literal hermite order is +0.20% there and the cell is over either way.
limits.evidence: plan/search.py, exhaustive per (L, n_batches) and recorded in data/scoreboards/jengine/searched_cuts.json. SEARCHED: every shared contiguous cut (C(L, k - 1), at most 120 per cell) crossed with plan/recovery.py's 26 structured seed orders, at most 3120 full plans per cell (partition, MILD DAG per batch, sieve, PlanCost). OBJECTIVE, stated before scoring and not tuned to it: feasible if max targets <= the cell's minimax + 1 (the minimax tolerance), then fewest max intermediates, then fewest FLOPs; ties to the lowest cut, then seed_orders() order. RESULT: Table 1 21/40 over, Table 2 3/40, Table 3 0/40 (the first search, cut only and minimax tolerance 0, had 30, 13, 0 and a worst margin of +7.50% at (15, 9) Table 2; the tolerance closes that cell in all three tables). UNREACHABLE, independent of the objective: in every residual cell, NO candidate in the whole searched space -- any cut, any of the 26 orders, any number of targets -- is at or under the printed value in all three tables at once; in each the smallest FLOPs any feasible candidate reaches is still over Table 1. NOT SEARCHED: per-direction cuts, seed orders outside the structured family, the sieve's re-expansion choice and sweep (the jengine/table1 record above searched those against exact_given_inputs and stopped at 17/40), and no-sieve.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the cells above, with their margin in percent over the printed value; their printed values are taken from the tables as published

limits.claim: [JEngine, v2, §4.1]'s comparison of MILD against Johnson et al.'s near-optimal tree search (the paper's refs 59/60): MILD 1-2% behind on FLOPs and 2-6% ahead on intermediates. Not reproducible on this machine; this repo's own measurement replaces it rather than reproducing it.
limits.mechanism: The search the paper compares against is not here: neither its code nor its output is available, and the paper does not state the grid, the cost convention or the reference point on a frontier that its percentages were taken against. A number computed here therefore measures a different comparison -- this tree's optimum (plan/optimum.py, exact over one reduction direction per materialised node with nodes shared; no algebraic rewriting, no recompute) under this tree's cost model (plan/cost.py) -- and cannot confirm or refute the printed one, only stand in its place.
limits.evidence: data/literature/jengine/mild_vs_optimum.json, recomputed by test/test_mild_vs_optimum.py (#111). Exact range L = 0..5: MILD equals the optimum for L <= 4 and at L = 5 is (51, 161) against (48, 160), behind on both axes, +6.25% intermediates and +0.625% FLOPs -- not the paper's shape (behind on FLOPs, ahead on intermediates). Every exact frontier there is a single point, so no scheme in the space is ahead of it on either axis. On the published grid a width-16 beam proves MILD at least 0.743% and 0.73% behind on FLOPs at L = 11 and 12 (dominated on both axes) and proves nothing elsewhere.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the paper's percentages are taken as published; this repo's gap is recorded beside them, not reconciled with them. No scoreboard, no rule: board and rule are null.

limits.claim: jengine/batching-crosses-our-ridge, #114's own claim: does batching move OUR [p|q] kernels across OUR cards' ridge? Answered on sm_86 only. gfx1200's answer is ABSENT (could not measure), and no answer here says anything about [JEngine, v2, Fig. 7]'s A100 result, which stands as the paper's and is not ours to dispute.
limits.mechanism: (1) THE RIDGE IS THE CARD'S. A verdict is intensity against peak fp64 over bandwidth, and our measured ridges -- 0.65 FLOP/B on sm_86 and 1.49 on gfx1200, ACHIEVABLE rates from this box's probes (data/measured/ceilings.json, #109), not datasheet peaks -- are each that card's; Fig. 7's A100 ridge is a different number, from a different card, and no comparison is drawn with it. Consumer fp64 is cut hard on both of our cards, so a class may be compute-bound ALREADY AT ONE BATCH here, and on sm_86 three of the four subgrid L are: that is a statement about the card, not about batching, and not a contradiction of the paper. (2) THE AMD ANSWER IS ABSENT. gfx1200 has no counter rows (measured_store.UNMEASURED, #112): rocprofv3 1.1.0 cannot load libdw.so.1 / libhsa-amd-aqlprofile64.so.1 in this container, and gfx1200 exposes no fp64 instruction counter in rocprofiler-sdk, so even a working profiler gives no measured FLOP count and hence no measured intensity. Could not measure is recorded as such, never as 'never crossed'. (3) WHAT THE INTENSITY SEES. The bytes are ncu's DRAM traffic (32-byte sectors) on ONE input, #53's wide-T (2048 x 128), in a counter run that serialises and replays each kernel; a batch whose working set stays in L2 hardly touches DRAM, so a split cell's kernel intensities spread over orders of magnitude, and another input or cache could move a verdict near the ridge. The verdict is a threshold, not a margin: L = 13 at 1 batch is compute-bound at 0.96 FLOP/B against 0.65. (4) WHICH CLASSES. SUBGRID's L are 7, 10, 13 and 16, with b in {1, 3, 6, 9, 12}: L = 10 is Fig. 7's [5|5], L = 13 and 16 bracket its [7|7], and [6|6] (L = 12) is not measured (#112 measured the compile cost and declined it). (5) THE PER-KERNEL VARIANT AT ONE BATCH IS THE CELL: a one-batch partition is one kernel, so the two variants can differ only past 1 batch; on sm_86 they do not differ at all. (6) WHAT THE FLOPS COUNT (#116). The numerator is every fp64 instruction the kernel issues (ncu's dadd + dmul + 2 dfma), the Boys evaluation included, whereas [JEngine, v2, Table 1]'s FLOPs exclude the Boys function; an intensity here is not Table 1's FLOPs over any byte count, and the counter run, which serialises and replays each kernel, is not the timed run (counter_ns is never a timing). (7) THE CEILINGS ARE ACHIEVABLE RATES, and one published figure is an assumption (#116): the ridges come from this box's probes, not datasheets, and gfx1200's published fp64 figure (0.801 TFLOPS, the probe's sanity bound only) assumes RDNA4's fp32 dual-issue applies to fp64; without that assumption the single-issue figure (~0.400 TFLOPS) sits below the recorded 0.446, so the bound would be wrong, not the probe (data/measured/ceilings.json, published.gfx1200.note). The recorded ceiling, and the 1.49 FLOP/B ridge computed from it, are the measurement either way; gfx1200 has no verdict to move.
limits.evidence: felizjueves.ridge over data/measured/roofline.json (124 kernel rows, 20 cells, sm_86, ncu 2025.3.1.0, recorded by #112 behind the card gate), recomputed by test/test_ridge.py::test_batching_crosses_our_ridge_on_sm_86_and_gfx1200_could_not_measure. sm_86, both variants identical: L = 7, 10, 13 compute-bound already at 1 batch (300, 3.54, 0.96 FLOP/B), compute-bound at every higher count too; L = 16 memory-bound at 1 batch (0.40 FLOP/B) and crossed at 3 (cell 1.52 FLOP/B, smallest kernel 1.46), compute-bound at 6, 9, 12 as well. gfx1200: could not measure. CROSS-READ AGAINST #60 (9 batches do not suffice on either card): on sm_86 every kernel of every 9-batch cell is compute-bound, so the roofline does NOT explain #60's verdict as kernels still memory-bound at 9 -- it contradicts that reading. sm_86's 9 fails #60 only on SPILL (12 spills less at L = 13 and 16) while 12 is slower than 9 at every L on both inputs; the roofline agrees with the clock there, since there is no ridge left to cross at 9. On gfx1200, where 12 wins on near-T at L = 16, the roofline can say nothing: no rows.
